title: Tio's method of keeping time with the foot
summary: Tio taught foot-tapping for time, then to feel it internally.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Was there any particular thing that Lorenzo would teach you? For instance, would he teach you anything about tapping your foot? Yes.

He did teach how to keep in time. He said, of course, as time go along, he wanted us to count with our footmen that he would teach us. That was to keep us right there that we wouldn't vary. He said, but then we must remember after we reached a certain stage and if we ever got to where we were playing professional music that that thing would stop. We must memorize those kind of things, or just have that feel for it.

And more or less keep time in your head. That's right. Well I know when I go to Mineta he teach me with my foot to tap on one and lift it up on two, down on three, and up on four. Well yes, that's the method that they taught, but Lorenzo didn't teach me that method.
Those that was taking lessons with him during that time, it was down on one, left on two, right on three, and up on four. That's the way he taught us. One, two, three. One, two, three.

One, two, three. One and two and two and three. That's the way he taught us. That's the way he taught us. And then other times, you know, like when it was waltz time or two or eight or two four, it would always be just the way he would do. One, two, three, four, one, two, three. One and two and three. That's the way he taught us.
